svg.text: The rival's glare: frame C, eyes fully hidden

Approved by Orb (2026-10-04): glasses frame C, the bare wedge; when the glare is on it hides his eyes completely. To Legal's rules (RL-066, RL-068): one hard-edged pale-violet wedge, never white, held 0.4 s at
The glare in time: a quick attack, a hold of 0.4 s at most, a release (one slow fade in and out, no strobing)
Close-up, then gameplay size (the figure is about 100 px tall): clear and glare
the head enlarged 6 times: lens clear, then glare (the eye is gone)
At gameplay size the glare is a pale violet bar
across the face where the eye was: one clear
change at one place. At the close-up size the lens
is fully opaque with one hard-edged wedge.
Small sizes: 72, 24 and the 12 px band, in colour and in grey (the violet stays visible; nothing reads as white)
the lens as one mean tint (about 30% wedge)

The glare stays in his violet (hue 265 to 264), at saturation 70 to 79 percent and lightness 78 to 87 percent: bright, but 20 points of lightness under white and clearly coloured, so at 24 px the mean tint is #c7aaf1, not white.
It is never gold, orange, red or white (RL-066).

Checked in code, not by eye: sampling the outline of his eye at five openness values (from shut to the widest shock), 30 of 30 of the points lie under the opaque lens, so no eye shows when the glare is on. To get all of them,

frame C's lens is about 7 percent taller than the first drawing of it (the shape and the thin rim are unchanged). The glare is also opaque on the far lens, and the lens sits in front of the eyes, so the render order is: face,
Rules for VFX and Animation (RL-066, RL-068)
A quick attack (about 120 ms), a hold of 0.4 s at most, a release (about 80 ms). One glare in any 3 s at most; key moments only: reading a move, pride, a taunt, the seal break. Never every exchange.

The glare is one hard-edged wedge in the pale violet, never white, gold, orange or red; no disc and no star; it counts as no mark under the stacking rule when it is not at a transformation break and has no shouted form name.
One slow fade in and out, no strobing (photosensitivity); with reduced motion it is a held tint with no sweep. The glasses themselves are never a display: no readout or scan bar on a lens.
Gesture: a nudge at the temple arm, or with the back of the forearm plate. The glare fires on the nudge. Never one finger at the bridge; never folded or steepled hands before the face.
Legal screen of this sheet: pending. The question left for Orb: none for the glare (decided); the glasses always on, or only for the taunt and the seal break, is still open.
